chunks: Beware; the earth which bears you, and the sky which overshadows you, are obedient to their Lord,
and they have not been bestowing their blessings on you for any feeling of pity on you or inclination towards you, nor for any good which they expect from you,
but they were commanded to bestow benefits on you and they are obeying, and were asked to maintain your good and so they are maintaining it.
ai.seo_question: Why do the earth and sky serve humans according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from the Prayer for Rain, Imam Ali (AS) emphasizes the cosmic humility of creation, noting that the earth and sky serve humanity not out of love or anticipation of reward, but solely through obedient submission to God's command. This reflects the Shia theological understanding of *'ibadah* (worship) as universal obedience, where natural phenomena act as conscious servants executing divine will for human benefit.
